# OpenACP

Self-hosted bridge that lets you interact with AI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, etc.) from messaging platforms (Telegram, Discord, etc.) via the [Agent Client Protocol (ACP)](https://agentclientprotocol.org/).

**One message, any channel, any agent.**

## How It Works

```
You (Telegram / Discord / ...)
  │
  ▼
OpenACP (ChannelAdapter)
  │
  ▼
ACP Protocol (JSON-RPC over stdio)
  │
  ▼
AI Agent subprocess (Claude Code, Codex, ...)
```

You send a message in Telegram → OpenACP forwards it to an AI coding agent via ACP → agent responds with text, code, tool calls → OpenACP streams the response back to your chat.

## Features

- **Multi-agent** — Switch between Claude Code, Codex, or any ACP-compatible agent
- **Telegram integration** — Forum topics per session, real-time streaming, inline permission buttons
- **Session management** — Multiple parallel sessions, prompt queue, auto-naming
- **Assistant topic** — AI-powered help bot that guides you through creating sessions
- **Notification topic** — Aggregated notifications with deep links
- **Workspace management** — Named workspaces or custom paths
- **Self-hosted** — Your keys, your data, your machine

## Quick Start

### Prerequisites

- Node.js >= 20
- pnpm
- A Telegram bot token (from [@BotFather](https://t.me/BotFather))
- A Telegram Supergroup with **Forum/Topics enabled**
- At least one ACP agent installed (e.g., `claude-agent-acp`)

### Install

```bash
git clone https://github.com/your-username/OpenACP.git
cd OpenACP
pnpm install
pnpm build
```

### Configure

Run once to generate the default config:

```bash
node packages/core/dist/main.js
```

Edit `~/.openacp/config.json`:

```json
{
  "channels": {
    "telegram": {
      "enabled": true,
      "botToken": "YOUR_BOT_TOKEN",
      "chatId": -100YOUR_CHAT_ID
    }
  },
  "agents": {
    "claude": {
      "command": "claude-agent-acp",
      "args": []
    }
  },
  "defaultAgent": "claude"
}
```

### Setup Telegram

1. Create a Supergroup in Telegram
2. Enable **Topics** in group settings
3. Add your bot as **admin** with **Manage Topics** permission
4. Get the chat ID (use [@raw_data_bot](https://t.me/raw_data_bot) or similar)

### Run

```bash
node packages/core/dist/main.js
```

OpenACP will auto-create two topics in your group:
- **📋 Notifications** — aggregated alerts with deep links
- **🤖 Assistant** — AI helper for managing sessions

## Usage

### Commands

| Command | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| `/new [agent] [workspace]` | Create a new session |
| `/new_chat` | New session, same agent & workspace |
| `/cancel` | Cancel current session |
| `/status` | Show session or system status |
| `/agents` | List available agents |
| `/help` | Show help |

### Examples

```
/new claude my-app          → New session with Claude in ~/openacp-workspace/my-app/
/new codex api-server       → New session with Codex in ~/openacp-workspace/api-server/
/new claude ~/code/project  → New session with absolute path
/new                        → New session with default agent and workspace
```

### Session Flow

1. Type `/new claude my-project` — bot creates a new topic
2. Send your coding request in the topic
3. Agent responds with streaming text, tool calls, and code
4. When agent needs permission (run command, edit file) → inline buttons appear
5. Click Allow/Deny → agent continues
6. `/cancel` to stop, or start a new topic with `/new`

## Configuration

Config file: `~/.openacp/config.json`

```json
{
  "channels": {
    "telegram": {
      "enabled": true,
      "botToken": "...",
      "chatId": -1001234567890,
      "notificationTopicId": null,
      "assistantTopicId": null
    }
  },
  "agents": {
    "claude": {
      "command": "claude-agent-acp",
      "args": [],
      "env": {}
    },
    "codex": {
      "command": "codex",
      "args": ["--acp"],
      "env": {}
    }
  },
  "defaultAgent": "claude",
  "workspace": {
    "baseDir": "~/openacp-workspace"
  },
  "security": {
    "allowedUserIds": [],
    "maxConcurrentSessions": 5,
    "sessionTimeoutMinutes": 60
  }
}
```

### Environment Variables

| Variable | Overrides |
|----------|-----------|
| `OPENACP_CONFIG_PATH` | Config file location |
| `OPENACP_TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` | `channels.telegram.botToken` |
| `OPENACP_TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID` | `channels.telegram.chatId` |
| `OPENACP_DEFAULT_AGENT` | `defaultAgent` |
| `OPENACP_DEBUG` | Enable debug logging (set to `1`) |

## Project Structure

```
openacp/
  packages/
    core/                      → @openacp/core
      src/
        main.ts                → Entry point
        core.ts                → OpenACPCore orchestrator
        config.ts              → ConfigManager + Zod validation
        session.ts             → Session (prompt queue, auto-name)
        agent-instance.ts      → ACP SDK integration
        channel.ts             → ChannelAdapter abstract class
        types.ts               → Shared types
    adapters/
      telegram/                → @openacp/adapter-telegram
        src/
          adapter.ts           → TelegramAdapter
          streaming.ts         → Real-time message streaming
          commands.ts          → Bot commands
          permissions.ts       → Permission inline buttons
          assistant.ts         → AI assistant topic
          formatting.ts        → Markdown → Telegram HTML
          topics.ts            → Forum topic management
```

## Roadmap

- **Phase 1** ✅ Core + Telegram + ACP agents
- **Phase 2** — Web UI, CLI, Discord adapter, tunnel/file viewer
- **Phase 3** — Agent skills as commands, session persistence
- **Phase 4** — Voice control, file sharing
- **Phase 5** — WhatsApp, agent chaining, plugin marketplace

See [docs/specs/01-roadmap.md](docs/specs/01-roadmap.md) for details.

## Adding a Channel Adapter

Extend `ChannelAdapter` from `@openacp/core`:

```typescript
import { ChannelAdapter } from '@openacp/core'

class MyAdapter extends ChannelAdapter {
  async start() { /* connect to platform */ }
  async stop() { /* disconnect */ }
  async sendMessage(sessionId, content) { /* send to user */ }
  async sendPermissionRequest(sessionId, request) { /* show buttons */ }
  async sendNotification(notification) { /* notify user */ }
  async createSessionThread(sessionId, name) { /* create thread */ }
  async renameSessionThread(sessionId, name) { /* rename thread */ }
}
```

## License

AGPL-3.0

Dự án **OpenACP** là một **cầu nối self-hosted** cho phép bạn tương tác với các AI coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, v.v.) từ các nền tảng nhắn tin (Telegram, Discord, v.v.) thông qua giao thức **ACP (Agent Client Protocol)**.

**Luồng hoạt động:**

```
Bạn (Telegram / Discord / ...)
  → OpenACP (ChannelAdapter)
    → ACP Protocol (JSON-RPC over stdio)
      → AI Agent subprocess (Claude Code, Codex, ...)
```

**Tính năng chính:**
- **Multi-agent** — Chuyển đổi giữa Claude Code, Codex, hoặc bất kỳ agent ACP nào
- **Tích hợp Telegram** — Mỗi session là một forum topic, streaming real-time, nút approve/deny inline
- **Quản lý session** — Nhiều session song song, hàng đợi prompt, tự đặt tên
- **Assistant topic** — Bot trợ giúp hướng dẫn tạo session
- **Workspace management** — Đường dẫn tùy chỉnh hoặc workspace có tên
- **Self-hosted** — Key của bạn, data của bạn, máy của bạn

**Cấu trúc:** Monorepo với pnpm workspace, gồm `@openacp/core` (orchestrator chính) và `@openacp/adapter-telegram` (adapter Telegram).

**Roadmap:** Phase 1 (Core + Telegram) đã xong. Các phase sau sẽ thêm Web UI, Discord, CLI, voice control, WhatsApp, v.v.

Nói ngắn gọn: bạn nhắn tin trên Telegram → OpenACP chuyển cho AI agent xử lý → kết quả stream ngược lại chat của bạn. Rất tiện để code từ điện thoại hoặc bất kỳ đâu có Telegram.

# Brainstorming Ideas Into Designs

Help turn ideas into fully formed designs and specs through natural collaborative dialogue.

Start by understanding the current project context, then ask questions one at a time to refine the idea. Once you understand what you're building, present the design and get user approval.

<HARD-GATE>
Do NOT invoke any implementation skill, write any code, scaffold any project, or take any implementation action until you have presented a design and the user has approved it. This applies to EVERY project regardless of perceived simplicity.
</HARD-GATE>

## Anti-Pattern: "This Is Too Simple To Need A Design"

Every project goes through this process. A todo list, a single-function utility, a config change — all of them. "Simple" projects are where unexamined assumptions cause the most wasted work. The design can be short (a few sentences for truly simple projects), but you MUST present it and get approval.

## Checklist

You MUST create a task for each of these items and complete them in order:

1. **Explore project context** — check files, docs, recent commits
2. **Offer visual companion** (if topic will involve visual questions) — this is its own message, not combined with a clarifying question. See the Visual Companion section below.
3. **Ask clarifying questions** — one at a time, understand purpose/constraints/success criteria
4. **Propose 2-3 approaches** — with trade-offs and your recommendation
5. **Present design** — in sections scaled to their complexity, get user approval after each section
6. **Write design doc** — save to `docs/superpowers/specs/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>-design.md` and commit
7. **Spec review loop** — dispatch spec-document-reviewer subagent with precisely crafted review context (never your session history); fix issues and re-dispatch until approved (max 3 iterations, then surface to human)
8. **User reviews written spec** — ask user to review the spec file before proceeding
9. **Transition to implementation** — invoke writing-plans skill to create implementation plan

## Process Flow

```dot
digraph brainstorming {
    "Explore project context" [shape=box];
    "Visual questions ahead?" [shape=diamond];
    "Offer Visual Companion\n(own message, no other content)" [shape=box];
    "Ask clarifying questions" [shape=box];
    "Propose 2-3 approaches" [shape=box];
    "Present design sections" [shape=box];
    "User approves design?" [shape=diamond];
    "Write design doc" [shape=box];
    "Spec review loop" [shape=box];
    "Spec review passed?" [shape=diamond];
    "User reviews spec?" [shape=diamond];
    "Invoke writing-plans skill" [shape=doublecircle];

    "Explore project context" -> "Visual questions ahead?";
    "Visual questions ahead?" -> "Offer Visual Companion\n(own message, no other content)" [label="yes"];
    "Visual questions ahead?" -> "Ask clarifying questions" [label="no"];
    "Offer Visual Companion\n(own message, no other content)" -> "Ask clarifying questions";
    "Ask clarifying questions" -> "Propose 2-3 approaches";
    "Propose 2-3 approaches" -> "Present design sections";
    "Present design sections" -> "User approves design?";
    "User approves design?" -> "Present design sections" [label="no, revise"];
    "User approves design?" -> "Write design doc" [label="yes"];
    "Write design doc" -> "Spec review loop";
    "Spec review loop" -> "Spec review passed?";
    "Spec review passed?" -> "Spec review loop" [label="issues found,\nfix and re-dispatch"];
    "Spec review passed?" -> "User reviews spec?" [label="approved"];
    "User reviews spec?" -> "Write design doc" [label="changes requested"];
    "User reviews spec?" -> "Invoke writing-plans skill" [label="approved"];
}
```

**The terminal state is invoking writing-plans.** Do NOT invoke frontend-design, mcp-builder, or any other implementation skill. The ONLY skill you invoke after brainstorming is writing-plans.

## The Process

**Understanding the idea:**

- Check out the current project state first (files, docs, recent commits)
- Before asking detailed questions, assess scope: if the request describes multiple independent subsystems (e.g., "build a platform with chat, file storage, billing, and analytics"), flag this immediately. Don't spend questions refining details of a project that needs to be decomposed first.
- If the project is too large for a single spec, help the user decompose into sub-projects: what are the independent pieces, how do they relate, what order should they be built? Then brainstorm the first sub-project through the normal design flow. Each sub-project gets its own spec → plan → implementation cycle.
- For appropriately-scoped projects, ask questions one at a time to refine the idea
- Prefer multiple choice questions when possible, but open-ended is fine too
- Only one question per message - if a topic needs more exploration, break it into multiple questions
- Focus on understanding: purpose, constraints, success criteria

**Exploring approaches:**

- Propose 2-3 different approaches with trade-offs
- Present options conversationally with your recommendation and reasoning
- Lead with your recommended option and explain why

**Presenting the design:**

- Once you believe you understand what you're building, present the design
- Scale each section to its complexity: a few sentences if straightforward, up to 200-300 words if nuanced
- Ask after each section whether it looks right so far
- Cover: architecture, components, data flow, error handling, testing
- Be ready to go back and clarify if something doesn't make sense

**Design for isolation and clarity:**

- Break the system into smaller units that each have one clear purpose, communicate through well-defined interfaces, and can be understood and tested independently
- For each unit, you should be able to answer: what does it do, how do you use it, and what does it depend on?
- Can someone understand what a unit does without reading its internals? Can you change the internals without breaking consumers? If not, the boundaries need work.
- Smaller, well-bounded units are also easier for you to work with - you reason better about code you can hold in context at once, and your edits are more reliable when files are focused. When a file grows large, that's often a signal that it's doing too much.

**Working in existing codebases:**

- Explore the current structure before proposing changes. Follow existing patterns.
- Where existing code has problems that affect the work (e.g., a file that's grown too large, unclear boundaries, tangled responsibilities), include targeted improvements as part of the design - the way a good developer improves code they're working in.
- Don't propose unrelated refactoring. Stay focused on what serves the current goal.

## After the Design

**Documentation:**

- Write the validated design (spec) to `docs/superpowers/specs/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>-design.md`
  - (User preferences for spec location override this default)
- Use elements-of-style:writing-clearly-and-concisely skill if available
- Commit the design document to git

**Spec Review Loop:**
After writing the spec document:

1. Dispatch spec-document-reviewer subagent (see spec-document-reviewer-prompt.md)
2. If Issues Found: fix, re-dispatch, repeat until Approved
3. If loop exceeds 3 iterations, surface to human for guidance

**User Review Gate:**
After the spec review loop passes, ask the user to review the written spec before proceeding:

> "Spec written and committed to `<path>`. Please review it and let me know if you want to make any changes before we start writing out the implementation plan."

Wait for the user's response. If they request changes, make them and re-run the spec review loop. Only proceed once the user approves.

**Implementation:**

- Invoke the writing-plans skill to create a detailed implementation plan
- Do NOT invoke any other skill. writing-plans is the next step.

## Key Principles

- **One question at a time** - Don't overwhelm with multiple questions
- **Multiple choice preferred** - Easier to answer than open-ended when possible
- **YAGNI ruthlessly** - Remove unnecessary features from all designs
- **Explore alternatives** - Always propose 2-3 approaches before settling
- **Incremental validation** - Present design, get approval before moving on
- **Be flexible** - Go back and clarify when something doesn't make sense

## Visual Companion

A browser-based companion for showing mockups, diagrams, and visual options during brainstorming. Available as a tool — not a mode. Accepting the companion means it's available for questions that benefit from visual treatment; it does NOT mean every question goes through the browser.

**Offering the companion:** When you anticipate that upcoming questions will involve visual content (mockups, layouts, diagrams), offer it once for consent:
> "Some of what we're working on might be easier to explain if I can show it to you in a web browser. I can put together mockups, diagrams, comparisons, and other visuals as we go. This feature is still new and can be token-intensive. Want to try it? (Requires opening a local URL)"

**This offer MUST be its own message.** Do not combine it with clarifying questions, context summaries, or any other content. The message should contain ONLY the offer above and nothing else. Wait for the user's response before continuing. If they decline, proceed with text-only brainstorming.

**Per-question decision:** Even after the user accepts, decide FOR EACH QUESTION whether to use the browser or the terminal. The test: **would the user understand this better by seeing it than reading it?**

# Brainstorming Ideas Into Designs

Help turn ideas into fully formed designs and specs through natural collaborative dialogue.

Start by understanding the current project context, then ask questions one at a time to refine the idea. Once you understand what you're building, present the design and get user approval.

<HARD-GATE>
Do NOT invoke any implementation skill, write any code, scaffold any project, or take any implementation action until you have presented a design and the user has approved it. This applies to EVERY project regardless of perceived simplicity.
</HARD-GATE>

## Anti-Pattern: "This Is Too Simple To Need A Design"

Every project goes through this process. A todo list, a single-function utility, a config change — all of them. "Simple" projects are where unexamined assumptions cause the most wasted work. The design can be short (a few sentences for truly simple projects), but you MUST present it and get approval.

## Checklist

You MUST create a task for each of these items and complete them in order:

1. **Explore project context** — check files, docs, recent commits
2. **Offer visual companion** (if topic will involve visual questions) — this is its own message, not combined with a clarifying question. See the Visual Companion section below.
3. **Ask clarifying questions** — one at a time, understand purpose/constraints/success criteria
4. **Propose 2-3 approaches** — with trade-offs and your recommendation
5. **Present design** — in sections scaled to their complexity, get user approval after each section
6. **Write design doc** — save to `docs/superpowers/specs/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>-design.md` and commit
7. **Spec review loop** — dispatch spec-document-reviewer subagent with precisely crafted review context (never your session history); fix issues and re-dispatch until approved (max 3 iterations, then surface to human)
8. **User reviews written spec** — ask user to review the spec file before proceeding
9. **Transition to implementation** — invoke writing-plans skill to create implementation plan

## Process Flow

```dot
digraph brainstorming {
    "Explore project context" [shape=box];
    "Visual questions ahead?" [shape=diamond];
    "Offer Visual Companion\n(own message, no other content)" [shape=box];
    "Ask clarifying questions" [shape=box];
    "Propose 2-3 approaches" [shape=box];
    "Present design sections" [shape=box];
    "User approves design?" [shape=diamond];
    "Write design doc" [shape=box];
    "Spec review loop" [shape=box];
    "Spec review passed?" [shape=diamond];
    "User reviews spec?" [shape=diamond];
    "Invoke writing-plans skill" [shape=doublecircle];

    "Explore project context" -> "Visual questions ahead?";
    "Visual questions ahead?" -> "Offer Visual Companion\n(own message, no other content)" [label="yes"];
    "Visual questions ahead?" -> "Ask clarifying questions" [label="no"];
    "Offer Visual Companion\n(own message, no other content)" -> "Ask clarifying questions";
    "Ask clarifying questions" -> "Propose 2-3 approaches";
    "Propose 2-3 approaches" -> "Present design sections";
    "Present design sections" -> "User approves design?";
    "User approves design?" -> "Present design sections" [label="no, revise"];
    "User approves design?" -> "Write design doc" [label="yes"];
    "Write design doc" -> "Spec review loop";
    "Spec review loop" -> "Spec review passed?";
    "Spec review passed?" -> "Spec review loop" [label="issues found,\nfix and re-dispatch"];
    "Spec review passed?" -> "User reviews spec?" [label="approved"];
    "User reviews spec?" -> "Write design doc" [label="changes requested"];
    "User reviews spec?" -> "Invoke writing-plans skill" [label="approved"];
}
```

**The terminal state is invoking writing-plans.** Do NOT invoke frontend-design, mcp-builder, or any other implementation skill. The ONLY skill you invoke after brainstorming is writing-plans.

## The Process

**Understanding the idea:**

- Check out the current project state first (files, docs, recent commits)
- Before asking detailed questions, assess scope: if the request describes multiple independent subsystems (e.g., "build a platform with chat, file storage, billing, and analytics"), flag this immediately. Don't spend questions refining details of a project that needs to be decomposed first.
- If the project is too large for a single spec, help the user decompose into sub-projects: what are the independent pieces, how do they relate, what order should they be built? Then brainstorm the first sub-project through the normal design flow. Each sub-project gets its own spec → plan → implementation cycle.
- For appropriately-scoped projects, ask questions one at a time to refine the idea
- Prefer multiple choice questions when possible, but open-ended is fine too
- Only one question per message - if a topic needs more exploration, break it into multiple questions
- Focus on understanding: purpose, constraints, success criteria

**Exploring approaches:**

- Propose 2-3 different approaches with trade-offs
- Present options conversationally with your recommendation and reasoning
- Lead with your recommended option and explain why

**Presenting the design:**

- Once you believe you understand what you're building, present the design
- Scale each section to its complexity: a few sentences if straightforward, up to 200-300 words if nuanced
- Ask after each section whether it looks right so far
- Cover: architecture, components, data flow, error handling, testing
- Be ready to go back and clarify if something doesn't make sense

**Design for isolation and clarity:**

- Break the system into smaller units that each have one clear purpose, communicate through well-defined interfaces, and can be understood and tested independently
- For each unit, you should be able to answer: what does it do, how do you use it, and what does it depend on?
- Can someone understand what a unit does without reading its internals? Can you change the internals without breaking consumers? If not, the boundaries need work.
- Smaller, well-bounded units are also easier for you to work with - you reason better about code you can hold in context at once, and your edits are more reliable when files are focused. When a file grows large, that's often a signal that it's doing too much.

**Working in existing codebases:**

- Explore the current structure before proposing changes. Follow existing patterns.
- Where existing code has problems that affect the work (e.g., a file that's grown too large, unclear boundaries, tangled responsibilities), include targeted improvements as part of the design - the way a good developer improves code they're working in.
- Don't propose unrelated refactoring. Stay focused on what serves the current goal.

## After the Design

**Documentation:**

- Write the validated design (spec) to `docs/superpowers/specs/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>-design.md`
  - (User preferences for spec location override this default)
- Use elements-of-style:writing-clearly-and-concisely skill if available
- Commit the design document to git

**Spec Review Loop:**
After writing the spec document:

1. Dispatch spec-document-reviewer subagent (see spec-document-reviewer-prompt.md)
2. If Issues Found: fix, re-dispatch, repeat until Approved
3. If loop exceeds 3 iterations, surface to human for guidance

**User Review Gate:**
After the spec review loop passes, ask the user to review the written spec before proceeding:

> "Spec written and committed to `<path>`. Please review it and let me know if you want to make any changes before we start writing out the implementation plan."

Wait for the user's response. If they request changes, make them and re-run the spec review loop. Only proceed once the user approves.

**Implementation:**

- Invoke the writing-plans skill to create a detailed implementation plan
- Do NOT invoke any other skill. writing-plans is the next step.

## Key Principles

- **One question at a time** - Don't overwhelm with multiple questions
- **Multiple choice preferred** - Easier to answer than open-ended when possible
- **YAGNI ruthlessly** - Remove unnecessary features from all designs
- **Explore alternatives** - Always propose 2-3 approaches before settling
- **Incremental validation** - Present design, get approval before moving on
- **Be flexible** - Go back and clarify when something doesn't make sense

## Visual Companion

A browser-based companion for showing mockups, diagrams, and visual options during brainstorming. Available as a tool — not a mode. Accepting the companion means it's available for questions that benefit from visual treatment; it does NOT mean every question goes through the browser.

**Offering the companion:** When you anticipate that upcoming questions will involve visual content (mockups, layouts, diagrams), offer it once for consent:
> "Some of what we're working on might be easier to explain if I can show it to you in a web browser. I can put together mockups, diagrams, comparisons, and other visuals as we go. This feature is still new and can be token-intensive. Want to try it? (Requires opening a local URL)"

**This offer MUST be its own message.** Do not combine it with clarifying questions, context summaries, or any other content. The message should contain ONLY the offer above and nothing else. Wait for the user's response before continuing. If they decline, proceed with text-only brainstorming.

**Per-question decision:** Even after the user accepts, decide FOR EACH QUESTION whether to use the browser or the terminal. The test: **would the user understand this better by seeing it than reading it?**

- **Use the browser** for content that IS visual — mockups, wireframes, layout comparisons, architecture diagrams, side-by-side visual designs
- **Use the terminal** for content that is text — requirements questions, conceptual choices, tradeoff lists, A/B/C/D text options, scope decisions

A question about a UI topic is not automatically a visual question. "What does personality mean in this context?" is a conceptual question — use the terminal. "Which wizard layout works better?" is a visual question — use the browser.

If they agree to the companion, read the detailed guide before proceeding:

    12→  await configManager.load()  // exits if config missing/invalid
    13→
    14→  const config = configManager.get()
    15→  log.info('Config loaded from', configManager['configPath'])
    16→
    17→  // 2. Create core
    18→  const core = new OpenACPCore(configManager)
    19→
    20→  // 3. Register enabled adapters
    21→  if (config.channels.telegram?.enabled) {
    22→    // Resolve adapter from workspace root (not from core's node_modules, to avoid circular dep)
    23→    const adapterPath = new URL('../../adapters/telegram/dist/index.js', import.meta.url).pathname
    24→    // @ts-ignore — dynamic path import
    25→    const { TelegramAdapter } = await import(adapterPath)
    26→    core.registerAdapter('telegram', new TelegramAdapter(core, config.channels.telegram))
    27→    log.info('Telegram adapter registered')
    28→  }
    29→
    30→  if (core.adapters.size === 0) {
    31→    log.error('No channels enabled. Enable at least one channel in config.')
    32→    process.exit(1)
    33→  }
    34→
    35→  // 4. Start
    36→  await core.start()
    37→
    38→  // 5. Log ready
    39→  const agents = Object.keys(config.agents).join(', ')
    40→  log.info(`OpenACP started. Agents: ${agents}`)
    41→  log.info('Press Ctrl+C to stop.')
    42→
    43→  // 6. Graceful shutdown
    44→  const shutdown = async (signal: string) => {
    45→    if (shuttingDown) return
    46→    shuttingDown = true
    47→    log.info(`${signal} received. Shutting down...`)
    48→
    49→    try {
    50→      await core.stop()
    51→    } catch (err) {
    52→      log.error('Error during shutdown:', err)
    53→    }
    54→
    55→    process.exit(0)
    56→  }
    57→
    58→  process.on('SIGINT', () => shutdown('SIGINT'))
    59→  process.on('SIGTERM', () => shutdown('SIGTERM'))
    60→
    61→  process.on('uncaughtException', (err) => {
    62→    log.error('Uncaught exception:', err)
    63→  })
    64→
    65→  process.on('unhandledRejection', (err) => {
    66→    log.error('Unhandled rejection:', err)
    67→  })
    68→}
    69→
    70→main().catch((err) => {
    71→  log.error('Fatal:', err)
    72→  process.exit(1)
    73→})
    74→

1→import { ConfigManager } from './config.js'
     2→import { AgentManager } from './agent-manager.js'
     3→import { SessionManager } from './session-manager.js'
     4→import { NotificationManager } from './notification.js'
     5→import { ChannelAdapter } from './channel.js'
     6→import { Session } from './session.js'
     7→import type { IncomingMessage, AgentEvent, OutgoingMessage, PermissionRequest } from './types.js'
     8→import { log } from './log.js'
     9→
    10→export class OpenACPCore {
    11→  configManager: ConfigManager
    12→  agentManager: AgentManager
    13→  sessionManager: SessionManager
    14→  notificationManager: NotificationManager
    15→  adapters: Map<string, ChannelAdapter> = new Map()
    16→
    17→  constructor(configManager: ConfigManager) {
    18→    this.configManager = configManager
    19→    const config = configManager.get()
    20→    this.agentManager = new AgentManager(config)
    21→    this.sessionManager = new SessionManager()
    22→    this.notificationManager = new NotificationManager(this.adapters)
    23→  }
    24→
    25→  registerAdapter(name: string, adapter: ChannelAdapter): void {
    26→    this.adapters.set(name, adapter)
    27→  }
    28→
    29→  async start(): Promise<void> {
    30→    for (const adapter of this.adapters.values()) {
    31→      await adapter.start()
    32→    }
    33→  }
    34→
    35→  async stop(): Promise<void> {
    36→    // 1. Notify users
    37→    try {
    38→      await this.notificationManager.notifyAll({
    39→        sessionId: 'system',
    40→        type: 'error',
    41→        summary: 'OpenACP is shutting down',
    42→      })
    43→    } catch { /* best effort */ }
    44→
    45→    // 2. Destroy all sessions
    46→    await this.sessionManager.destroyAll()
    47→
    48→    // 3. Stop adapters
    49→    for (const adapter of this.adapters.values()) {
    50→      await adapter.stop()
    51→    }
    52→  }
    53→
    54→  // --- Message Routing ---
    55→
    56→  async handleMessage(message: IncomingMessage): Promise<void> {
    57→    const config = this.configManager.get()
    58→
    59→    // Security: check allowed user IDs
    60→    if (config.security.allowedUserIds.length > 0) {
    61→      if (!config.security.allowedUserIds.includes(message.userId)) return
    62→    }
    63→
    64→    // Check concurrent session limit
    65→    const activeSessions = this.sessionManager.listSessions()
    66→      .filter(s => s.status === 'active' || s.status === 'initializing')
    67→    if (activeSessions.length >= config.security.maxConcurrentSessions) {
    68→      const adapter = this.adapters.get(message.channelId)
    69→      if (adapter) {
    70→        await adapter.sendMessage('system', {
    71→          type: 'error',
    72→          text: `Max concurrent sessions (${config.security.maxConcurrentSessions}) reached. Cancel a session first.`,
    73→        })
    74→      }
    75→      return
    76→    }
    77→
    78→    // Find session by thread
    79→    const session = this.sessionManager.getSessionByThread(message.channelId, message.threadId)
    80→    if (!session) return
    81→
    82→    // Forward to session
    83→    await session.enqueuePrompt(message.text)
    84→  }
    85→
    86→  async handleNewSession(
    87→    channelId: string,
    88→    agentName?: string,
    89→    workspacePath?: string,
    90→  ): Promise<Session> {
    91→    const config = this.configManager.get()
    92→    const resolvedAgent = agentName || config.defaultAgent
    93→    const resolvedWorkspace = this.configManager.resolveWorkspace(
    94→      workspacePath || config.agents[resolvedAgent]?.workingDirectory
    95→    )
    96→
    97→    const session = await this.sessionManager.createSession(
    98→      channelId, resolvedAgent, resolvedWorkspace, this.agentManager
    99→    )
   100→
   101→    // Wire events
   102→    const adapter = this.adapters.get(channelId)
   103→    if (adapter) {
   104→      this.wireSessionEvents(session, adapter)
   105→    }
   106→
   107→    return session
   108→  }
   109→
   110→  async handleNewChat(
   111→    channelId: string,
   112→    currentThreadId: string,
   113→  ): Promise<Session | null> {
   114→    const currentSession = this.sessionManager.getSessionByThread(channelId, currentThreadId)
   115→    if (!currentSession) return null
   116→
   117→    return this.handleNewSession(
   118→      channelId,
   119→      currentSession.agentName,
   120→      currentSession.workingDirectory,
   121→    )
   122→  }
   123→
   124→  // --- Event Wiring ---
   125→
   126→  private toOutgoingMessage(event: AgentEvent): OutgoingMessage {
   127→    switch (event.type) {
   128→      case 'text':
   129→        return { type: 'text', text: event.content }
   130→      case 'thought':
   131→        return { type: 'thought', text: event.content }
   132→      case 'tool_call':
   133→        return { type: 'tool_call', text: event.name, metadata: { id: event.id, kind: event.kind, status: event.status, content: event.content, locations: event.locations } }
   134→      case 'tool_update':
   135→        return { type: 'tool_update', text: '', metadata: { id: event.id, status: event.status, content: event.content } }
   136→      case 'plan':
   137→        return { type: 'plan', text: '', metadata: { entries: event.entries } }
   138→      case 'usage':
   139→        return { type: 'usage', text: '', metadata: { tokensUsed: event.tokensUsed, contextSize: event.contextSize, cost: event.cost } }
   140→      case 'commands_update':
   141→        // Log but don't surface to user (Phase 3 feature)
   142→        log.debug('Commands update:', event.commands)
   143→        return { type: 'text', text: '' }  // no-op for now
   144→      default:
   145→        return { type: 'text', text: '' }
   146→    }
   147→  }
   148→
   149→  // Public — adapters call this for assistant session wiring
   150→  wireSessionEvents(session: Session, adapter: ChannelAdapter): void {
   151→    // Set adapter reference for autoName → renameSessionThread
   152→    session.adapter = adapter
   153→
   154→    session.agentInstance.onSessionUpdate = (event: AgentEvent) => {
   155→      switch (event.type) {
   156→        case 'text':
   157→        case 'thought':
   158→        case 'tool_call':
   159→        case 'tool_update':
   160→        case 'plan':
   161→        case 'usage':
   162→          adapter.sendMessage(session.id, this.toOutgoingMessage(event))
   163→          break
   164→
   165→        case 'session_end':
   166→          session.status = 'finished'
   167→          adapter.sendMessage(session.id, { type: 'session_end', text: `Done (${event.reason})` })
   168→          this.notificationManager.notify(session.channelId, {
   169→            sessionId: session.id,
   170→            sessionName: session.name,
   171→            type: 'completed',
   172→            summary: `Session "${session.name || session.id}" completed`,
   173→          })
   174→          break
   175→
   176→        case 'error':
   177→          adapter.sendMessage(session.id, { type: 'error', text: event.message })
   178→          this.notificationManager.notify(session.channelId, {
   179→            sessionId: session.id,
   180→            sessionName: session.name,
   181→            type: 'error',
   182→            summary: event.message,
   183→          })
   184→          break
   185→
   186→        case 'commands_update':
   187→          log.debug('Commands available:', event.commands)
   188→          break
   189→      }
   190→    }
   191→
   192→    session.agentInstance.onPermissionRequest = async (request: PermissionRequest) => {
   193→      // Send permission UI to session topic
   194→      await adapter.sendPermissionRequest(session.id, request)
   195→
   196→      // Send notification with deep link
   197→      await this.notificationManager.notify(session.channelId, {
   198→        sessionId: session.id,
   199→        sessionName: session.name,
   200→        type: 'permission',
   201→        summary: request.description,
   202→      })
   203→
   204→      // Wait for user response — adapter resolves this promise
   205→      return new Promise<string>((resolve) => {
   206→        session.pendingPermission = { requestId: request.id, resolve }
   207→      })
   208→    }
   209→  }
   210→}
   211→

1→# OpenACP — Configuration System
     2→
     3→## Overview
     4→
     5→Configuration is stored as a JSON file. It is the single source of truth for which channels, agents, and features are enabled. CLI and Web UI are interfaces that read/write this file.
     6→
     7→## Config File Location
     8→
     9→Default: `~/.openacp/config.json`
    10→
    11→Override via environment variable: `OPENACP_CONFIG_PATH`
    12→
    13→## Data Directory
    14→
    15→```
    16→~/.openacp/
    17→  config.json              → Main configuration file
    18→  data/
    19→    sessions/              → Session persistence (Phase 3)
    20→  logs/                    → Log files
    21→
    22→~/openacp-workspace/       → Default workspace base directory (separate from .openacp)
    23→```
    24→
    25→## Full Schema
    26→
    27→```json
    28→{
    29→  "channels": {
    30→    "telegram": {
    31→      "enabled": true,
    32→      "botToken": "123456:ABC-DEF...",
    33→      "chatId": -1001234567890,
    34→      "notificationTopicId": null,
    35→      "assistantTopicId": null
    36→    },
    37→    "discord": {
    38→      "enabled": false,
    39→      "botToken": "...",
    40→      "guildId": "...",
    41→      "forumChannelId": "...",
    42→      "notificationChannelId": null
    43→    }
    44→  },
    45→  "agents": {
    46→    "claude": {
    47→      "command": "claude-agent-acp",
    48→      "args": [],
    49→      "workingDirectory": "~/projects",
    50→      "env": {}
    51→    },
    52→    "codex": {
    53→      "command": "codex",
    54→      "args": ["--acp"],
    55→      "workingDirectory": "~/projects",
    56→      "env": {}
    57→    }
    58→  },
    59→  "defaultAgent": "claude",
    60→  "workspace": {
    61→    "baseDir": "~/openacp-workspace"
    62→  },
    63→  "tunnel": {
    64→    "provider": "cloudflare",
    65→    "options": {}
    66→  },
    67→  "security": {
    68→    "allowedUserIds": [],
    69→    "maxConcurrentSessions": 5,
    70→    "sessionTimeoutMinutes": 60,
    71→    "authToken": "auto-generated-on-first-run"
    72→  },
    73→  "server": {
    74→    "host": "127.0.0.1",
    75→    "port": 3100
    76→  },
    77→  "stt": {
    78→    "provider": "whisper",
    79→    "options": {
    80→      "apiKey": "",
    81→      "model": "whisper-1",
    82→      "language": "en"
    83→    }
    84→  },
    85→  "sessions": {
    86→    "retentionDays": 30,
    87→    "persistenceEnabled": false
    88→  }
    89→}
    90→```
    91→
    92→## Sections
    93→
    94→### `channels`
    95→
    96→Key-value map where key = channel adapter name, value = channel-specific config.
    97→
    98→Each channel adapter defines its own config schema. The core only requires:
    99→- `enabled: boolean` — whether to start this adapter
   100→
   101→All other fields are adapter-specific.
   102→
   103→### `agents`
   104→
   105→Key-value map where key = agent name (user-facing), value = agent config.
   106→
   107→| Field | Type | Required | Description |
   108→|-------|------|----------|-------------|
   109→| `command` | string | yes | Command to spawn the agent |
   110→| `args` | string[] | no | Command arguments |
   111→| `workingDirectory` | string | no | CWD for the agent subprocess |
   112→| `env` | Record<string, string> | no | Extra environment variables |
   113→
   114→### `defaultAgent`
   115→
   116→The agent name used when user runs `/new` without specifying an agent.
   117→
   118→### `workspace`
   119→
   120→Workspace directory management.
   121→
   122→| Field | Type | Required | Description |
   123→|-------|------|----------|-------------|
   124→| `baseDir` | string | no | Base directory for named workspaces (default: "~/openacp-workspace") |
   125→
   126→When user runs `/new agent my-app`, workspace resolves to `{baseDir}/my-app/` (lowercase).
   127→When user provides absolute path (`/path/to/project` or `~/project`), it's used directly.
   128→
   129→### `tunnel`
   130→
   131→Tunnel configuration for exposing local services (file viewer, web UI).
   132→
   133→| Field | Type | Required | Description |
   134→|-------|------|----------|-------------|
   135→| `provider` | string | no | Tunnel provider: "cloudflare", "ngrok", "bore" |
   136→| `options` | object | no | Provider-specific options |
   137→
   138→### `security`
   139→
   140→Access control and resource limits.
   141→
   142→| Field | Type | Required | Description |
   143→|-------|------|----------|-------------|
   144→| `allowedUserIds` | string[] | no | Whitelist of user IDs. Empty = all group members (default: []) |
   145→| `maxConcurrentSessions` | number | no | Max active agent subprocesses (default: 5) |
   146→| `sessionTimeoutMinutes` | number | no | Auto-cancel idle sessions (default: 60) |
   147→| `authToken` | string | no | Token for tunnel/web UI auth (auto-generated on first run) |
   148→
   149→### `server`
   150→
   151→Internal HTTP server config (used by file viewer and web UI).
   152→
   153→| Field | Type | Required | Description |
   154→|-------|------|----------|-------------|
   155→| `host` | string | no | Bind address (default: "127.0.0.1") |
   156→| `port` | number | no | Port (default: 3100) |
   157→
   158→### `stt` (Phase 4)
   159→
   160→Speech-to-text provider config for voice messages.
   161→
   162→| Field | Type | Required | Description |
   163→|-------|------|----------|-------------|
   164→| `provider` | string | no | STT provider: "whisper", "local-whisper", "google", "deepgram" |
   165→| `options` | object | no | Provider-specific options (apiKey, model, language) |
   166→
   167→### `sessions` (Phase 3)
   168→
   169→Session persistence settings.
   170→
   171→| Field | Type | Required | Description |
   172→|-------|------|----------|-------------|
   173→| `retentionDays` | number | no | Auto-cleanup sessions older than N days (default: 30) |
   174→| `persistenceEnabled` | boolean | no | Enable session save/resume (default: false) |
   175→
   176→## Environment Variable Overrides
   177→
   178→Sensitive values can be set via environment variables instead of the config file:
   179→
   180→| Variable | Overrides |
   181→|----------|-----------|
   182→| `OPENACP_CONFIG_PATH` | Config file location |
   183→| `OPENACP_TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` | `channels.telegram.botToken` |
   184→| `OPENACP_TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID` | `channels.telegram.chatId` |
   185→| `OPENACP_DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN` | `channels.discord.botToken` |
   186→| `OPENACP_DEFAULT_AGENT` | `defaultAgent` |
   187→
   188→Environment variables take precedence over config file values.
   189→
   190→## Validation
   191→
   192→Config is validated on load using a schema validator (e.g., Zod). Invalid config rejects startup with a clear error message indicating which field is invalid.
   193→
   194→## Hot Reload
   195→
   196→ConfigManager watches the config file for changes. When the file is modified:
   197→1. Re-validate the new config
   198→2. If valid, apply changes (start/stop adapters as needed)
   199→3. If invalid, log error and keep current config
   200→

1→# OpenACP — Product Overview
     2→
     3→## Vision
     4→
     5→OpenACP is a self-hosted bridge that lets users interact with any ACP-compatible AI coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, etc.) from any messaging platform (Telegram, Discord, WhatsApp, etc.).
     6→
     7→**One message, any channel, any agent.**
     8→
     9→## Core Concepts
    10→
    11→### Channel
    12→A messaging platform adapter (Telegram, Discord, WhatsApp...). Each channel implements the `ChannelAdapter` abstract class and can be plugged into the core system.
    13→
    14→### Agent
    15→An AI coding agent that speaks the ACP (Agent Client Protocol). Agents are spawned as subprocesses and communicate via JSON-RPC over stdio.
    16→
    17→### Session
    18→A single conversation between a user and an agent. Each session maps to a topic/thread on the channel. Sessions can run in parallel.
    19→
    20→### Notification Topic
    21→A dedicated topic/thread on the channel that aggregates notifications from all sessions. Contains summaries + deep links to the original session topics.
    22→
    23→## Architecture
    24→
    25→```
    26→User (Telegram / Discord / ...)
    27→  │
    28→  ▼
    29→ChannelAdapter (plugin)
    30→  │
    31→  ▼
    32→┌─────────────────────────────┐
    33→│         OpenACP Core        │
    34→│                             │
    35→│  SessionManager             │
    36→│  AgentManager               │
    37→│  ConfigManager              │
    38→│  NotificationManager        │
    39→└─────────────────────────────┘
    40→  │
    41→  ▼
    42→ACP SDK (@agentclientprotocol/sdk)
    43→  │
    44→  ▼
    45→AI Agent subprocess (stdio JSON-RPC)
    46→```
    47→
    48→## Tech Stack
    49→
    50→- **Language**: TypeScript
    51→- **Runtime**: Node.js
    52→- **ACP SDK**: `@agentclientprotocol/sdk` (official)
    53→- **Monorepo**: pnpm workspace
    54→- **Config**: JSON file
    55→
    56→## Project Structure
    57→
    58→```
    59→openacp/
    60→  packages/
    61→    core/                  → Abstract classes, managers, shared types
    62→    adapters/
    63→      telegram/            → Telegram channel adapter
    64→      discord/             → Discord channel adapter (Phase 2)
    65→      whatsapp/            → WhatsApp channel adapter (Phase 5)
    66→    agents/
    67→      claude/              → Claude Code agent config/wrapper
    68→      codex/               → Codex agent config/wrapper
    69→    cli/                   → CLI tool for config & management
    70→    web-ui/                → Web dashboard (Phase 2)
    71→```
    72→
    73→## Roadmap
    74→
    75→See [01-roadmap.md](./01-roadmap.md) for the full phased roadmap.
    76→
    77→## Spec Documents
    78→
    79→| Document | Description |
    80→|----------|-------------|
    81→| [00-overview.md](./00-overview.md) | This document — product overview |
    82→| [01-roadmap.md](./01-roadmap.md) | Phased roadmap |
    83→| [02-core-architecture.md](./02-core-architecture.md) | Core system design |
    84→| [03-config.md](./03-config.md) | Configuration system |
    85→| [features/telegram-adapter.md](./features/telegram-adapter.md) | Telegram channel adapter |
    86→| [features/discord-adapter.md](./features/discord-adapter.md) | Discord channel adapter |
    87→| [features/tunnel-service.md](./features/tunnel-service.md) | Tunnel & file viewer |
    88→| [features/skills-as-commands.md](./features/skills-as-commands.md) | Agent skills → channel commands |
    89→| [features/voice-control.md](./features/voice-control.md) | Voice message control |
    90→| [features/web-ui.md](./features/web-ui.md) | Web dashboard |
    91→| [features/cli.md](./features/cli.md) | CLI tool |
    92→| [features/session-persistence.md](./features/session-persistence.md) | Session persistence & resume |

1→# OpenACP — Core Architecture
     2→
     3→## Overview
     4→
     5→The core package (`packages/core/`) is the central hub. It defines abstract interfaces, manages sessions, spawns agents, and routes messages between channels and agents.
     6→
     7→## Core Types
     8→
     9→```typescript
    10→// Incoming message from channel to core
    11→interface IncomingMessage {
    12→  channelId: string
    13→  threadId: string
    14→  userId: string
    15→  text: string
    16→  attachments?: Attachment[]   // Phase 4: files, images
    17→  voiceAudio?: Buffer          // Phase 4: voice messages
    18→}
    19→
    20→interface Attachment {
    21→  type: 'file' | 'image'
    22→  name: string
    23→  url: string
    24→  mimeType: string
    25→}
    26→
    27→// Outgoing message from core to channel
    28→interface OutgoingMessage {
    29→  type: 'text' | 'tool_call' | 'tool_update' | 'session_end' | 'error'
    30→  text: string
    31→  metadata?: Record<string, unknown>
    32→}
    33→
    34→// Permission request forwarded from agent
    35→interface PermissionRequest {
    36→  id: string
    37→  description: string
    38→  options: PermissionOption[]
    39→}
    40→
    41→interface PermissionOption {
    42→  id: string
    43→  label: string
    44→  isAllow: boolean
    45→}
    46→
    47→// Notification sent to the notification topic/channel
    48→interface NotificationMessage {
    49→  sessionId: string
    50→  sessionName?: string
    51→  type: 'completed' | 'error' | 'permission' | 'input_required'
    52→  summary: string
    53→  deepLink?: string   // link to the specific message in session topic
    54→}
    55→
    56→// Agent events streamed from ACP agent
    57→type AgentEvent =
    58→  | { type: 'text'; content: string }
    59→  | { type: 'tool_call'; id: string; name: string; args: string; status: ToolCallStatus }
    60→  | { type: 'tool_update'; id: string; status: ToolCallStatus; output?: string }
    61→  | { type: 'permission_request'; request: PermissionRequest }
    62→  | { type: 'session_end'; reason: string }
    63→  | { type: 'error'; message: string }
    64→
    65→type ToolCallStatus = 'pending' | 'in_progress' | 'completed' | 'failed'
    66→
    67→// Agent definition from config
    68→interface AgentDefinition {
    69→  name: string
    70→  command: string
    71→  args: string[]
    72→  workingDirectory?: string
    73→  env?: Record<string, string>
    74→}
    75→
    76→// Session ID: nanoid (URL-safe, used in tunnel URLs)
    77→// Generated via nanoid(12) — e.g., "V1StGXR8_Z5j"
    78→```
    79→
    80→## Components
    81→
    82→### 1. ChannelAdapter (Abstract Class)
    83→
    84→The base class that all channel adapters must extend. Adapters receive platform events and call `core.handleMessage()` to forward them. Core calls adapter methods to send responses back.
    85→
    86→```typescript
    87→abstract class ChannelAdapter {
    88→  constructor(protected core: OpenACPCore, protected config: ChannelConfig) {}
    89→
    90→  // Lifecycle
    91→  abstract start(): Promise<void>
    92→  abstract stop(): Promise<void>
    93→
    94→  // Outgoing: core → channel
    95→  abstract sendMessage(sessionId: string, content: OutgoingMessage): Promise<void>
    96→  abstract sendPermissionRequest(sessionId: string, request: PermissionRequest): Promise<void>
    97→  abstract sendNotification(notification: NotificationMessage): Promise<void>
    98→
    99→  // Session lifecycle on the channel side
   100→  abstract createSessionThread(sessionId: string, name: string): Promise<string>  // returns threadId
   101→  abstract renameSessionThread(sessionId: string, newName: string): Promise<void>
   102→}
   103→```
   104→
   105→### 2. AgentManager
   106→
   107→Manages available agents and their subprocess lifecycle.
   108→
   109→**Responsibilities:**
   110→- Load agent definitions from config
   111→- Spawn ACP agent subprocesses (`child_process.spawn`)
   112→- Initialize ACP connection via `@agentclientprotocol/sdk`
   113→- Handle ACP handshake (capabilities exchange)
   114→- Terminate agent processes on session end
   115→
   116→**Interface:**
   117→```typescript
   118→class AgentManager {
   119→  constructor(private config: AgentsConfig) {}
   120→
   121→  getAvailableAgents(): AgentDefinition[]
   122→  spawn(agentName: string, workingDirectory: string): Promise<AgentInstance>
   123→  terminate(sessionId: string): Promise<void>
   124→}
   125→```
   126→
   127→**AgentInstance** wraps the ACP SDK connection:
   128→```typescript
   129→interface AgentInstance {
   130→  sessionId: string
   131→  agentName: string
   132→  onSessionUpdate: (event: AgentEvent) => void           // callback for streaming events
   133→  onPermissionRequest: (req: PermissionRequest) => Promise<string>  // callback for permissions
   134→  prompt(message: string): Promise<PromptResponse>        // blocking until turn completes
   135→  cancel(): Promise<void>
   136→  getSkills(): Promise<Skill[]>   // Phase 3
   137→  destroy(): Promise<void>
   138→}
   139→```
   140→
   141→### 3. SessionManager
   142→
   143→Maps channel threads to ACP sessions.
   144→
   145→**Responsibilities:**
   146→- Create new sessions (channel thread + agent instance)
   147→- Route messages from channel to correct agent
   148→- Route agent events back to correct channel thread
   149→- Track session state (initializing, active, cancelled, finished, error)
   150→- Auto-name sessions after first prompt
   151→
   152→**Interface:**
   153→```typescript
   154→class SessionManager {
   155→  createSession(channelId: string, agentName: string, workingDirectory: string): Promise<Session>
   156→  getSession(sessionId: string): Session | undefined
   157→  getSessionByThread(channelId: string, threadId: string): Session | undefined
   158→  cancelSession(sessionId: string): Promise<void>
   159→  listSessions(channelId?: string): Session[]
   160→}
   161→```
   162→
   163→**Session:**
   164→```typescript
   165→interface Session {
   166→  id: string                  // nanoid(12), URL-safe
   167→  channelId: string
   168→  threadId: string
   169→  agentName: string
   170→  workingDirectory: string
   171→  agentInstance: AgentInstance
   172→  status: 'initializing' | 'active' | 'cancelled' | 'finished' | 'error'
   173→  createdAt: Date
   174→  name?: string  // auto-named after first prompt
   175→}
   176→```
   177→
   178→### 4. ConfigManager
   179→
   180→Loads, validates, and provides access to the JSON config file.
   181→
   182→**Responsibilities:**
   183→- Load config from file path (default: `~/.openacp/config.json`)
   184→- Validate config schema
   185→- Provide typed access to config sections
   186→- Save config changes (for CLI/Web UI)
   187→- Watch for config file changes (hot reload)
   188→
   189→See [03-config.md](./03-config.md) for full config schema.
   190→
   191→### 5. NotificationManager
   192→
   193→Manages the notification topic/channel.
   194→
   195→**Responsibilities:**
   196→- Aggregate events from all sessions
   197→- Format notification messages (summary + deep link)
   198→- Route to the correct channel adapter's notification method
   199→- Determine which events deserve notification:
   200→  - Session completed
   201→  - Session error
   202→  - Permission request (with deep link to approve in session topic)
   203→  - Agent requires user input
   204→
   205→**Interface:**
   206→```typescript
   207→class NotificationManager {
   208→  constructor(private adapters: Map<string, ChannelAdapter>) {}
   209→
   210→  notify(channelId: string, notification: NotificationMessage): Promise<void>
   211→  notifyAll(notification: NotificationMessage): Promise<void>
   212→}
   213→
   214→### 6. OpenACPCore (Orchestrator)
   215→
   216→The main entry point that wires everything together.
   217→
   218→```typescript
   219→class OpenACPCore {
   220→  configManager: ConfigManager
   221→  agentManager: AgentManager
   222→  sessionManager: SessionManager
   223→  notificationManager: NotificationManager
   224→  adapters: Map<string, ChannelAdapter>
   225→
   226→  async start(): Promise<void>    // Load config, start all enabled adapters
   227→  async stop(): Promise<void>     // Graceful shutdown
   228→  registerAdapter(name: string, adapter: ChannelAdapter): void
   229→
   230→  // Inbound: adapters call this to forward user messages to core
   231→  async handleMessage(message: IncomingMessage): Promise<void>
   232→
   233→  // Inbound: adapters call this to forward permission responses
   234→  async handlePermissionResponse(sessionId: string, optionId: string): Promise<void>
   235→}
   236→```
   237→
   238→## Data Flow
   239→
   240→### User sends message
   241→
   242→```
   243→1. User types in channel topic/thread
   244→2. ChannelAdapter receives platform event, calls core.handleMessage(incomingMessage)
   245→3. SessionManager looks up session by channelId + threadId
   246→4. If no session → error (user must /new first)
   247→5. AgentInstance.prompt(message) → streams AgentEvents
   248→6. For each AgentEvent:
   249→   a. Text → adapter.sendMessage() (silent in topic)
   250→            → notificationManager (if significant)
   251→   b. ToolCall → adapter.sendMessage() (show status)
   252→   c. PermissionRequest → adapter.sendPermissionRequest() (inline buttons in topic)
   253→                        → notificationManager (summary + deep link)
   254→   d. SessionEnd → adapter.sendMessage() (final status)
   255→                 → notificationManager (completion notification)
   256→```
   257→
   258→### User creates new session
   259→
   260→```
   261→1. User types /new [agent-name] [working-directory] in channel
   262→2. ChannelAdapter parses command, calls core.handleMessage()
   263→3. Core resolves: agent (default if omitted), workingDirectory (agent default if omitted)
   264→4. SessionManager.createSession(channelId, agentName, workingDirectory)
   265→5. AgentManager.spawn(agentName, workingDirectory) → AgentInstance
   266→6. adapter.createSessionThread(sessionId, "New Session") → threadId
   267→7. Session is now active, waiting for first prompt
   268→8. After first prompt response → AI generates session name
   269→9. adapter.renameSessionThread(sessionId, generatedName)
   270→```
   271→
   272→## Security
   273→
   274→### User Authorization
   275→
   276→Since OpenACP is self-hosted, the trust boundary is the channel group/server itself:
   277→- **Telegram**: Only users in the configured Supergroup can interact with the bot
   278→- **Discord**: Only members of the configured guild/server
   279→
   280→Additional controls via config:
   281→```json
   282→{
   283→  "security": {
   284→    "allowedUserIds": [],
   285→    "maxConcurrentSessions": 5,
   286→    "sessionTimeoutMinutes": 60
   287→  }
   288→}
   289→```
   290→
   291→- `allowedUserIds`: Whitelist of user IDs. Empty = all group members allowed.
   292→- `maxConcurrentSessions`: Limit concurrent agent subprocesses (resource protection).
   293→- `sessionTimeoutMinutes`: Auto-cancel idle sessions.
   294→
   295→### Tunnel Security
   296→
   297→Tunnel URLs expose local services publicly. Default protections:
   298→- **Token auth**: Generated on startup, appended as query param or header. Stored in config.
   299→- File viewer only serves files within configured `workingDirectory` paths (path traversal prevention).
   300→- Read-only — no write endpoints on the file viewer.
   301→
   302→### Web UI Security
   303→
   304→- Default: token-based auth (same token as tunnel).
   305→- Config API (`PUT /api/config`) requires auth.
   306→- Bind to `127.0.0.1` by default (localhost only). External access only via tunnel with auth.
   307→
   308→### Agent Subprocess Isolation
   309→
   310→- Agents run with the same OS user as OpenACP (self-hosted assumption).
   311→- `workingDirectory` constrains where the agent operates.
   312→- Permission requests from agents are always forwarded to the user — core never auto-approves by default.
   313→
   314→## Error Handling
   315→
   316→- Agent subprocess crashes → Session status = 'error', notify user, offer to restart
   317→- Channel API errors → Retry with backoff, log errors
   318→- Config errors → Validate on load, reject invalid config with clear error messages
   319→- ACP protocol errors → Log and surface to user in session topic
   320→
   321→## Graceful Shutdown
   322→
   323→When `stop()` is called:
   324→1. Stop accepting new sessions
   325→2. Send SIGTERM to all active agent subprocesses
   326→3. Wait up to 10 seconds for agents to exit
   327→4. Force SIGKILL remaining agents
   328→5. Notify active sessions: "OpenACP is shutting down"
   329→6. Close all channel adapter connections
   330→7. Close HTTP server and tunnel
   331→

1→# Feature: CLI Tool
     2→
     3→**Phase**: 2
     4→**Package**: `packages/cli/`
     5→
     6→## Overview
     7→
     8→Command-line tool for managing OpenACP — configure channels/agents, start/stop the daemon, view sessions.
     9→
    10→## Commands
    11→
    12→```
    13→openacp start                    # Start OpenACP daemon
    14→openacp stop                     # Stop daemon
    15→openacp status                   # Show daemon status + active sessions
    16→
    17→openacp config show              # Print current config
    18→openacp config set <key> <value> # Set config value
    19→openacp config edit              # Open config in $EDITOR
    20→
    21→openacp agents list              # List configured agents
    22→openacp agents add <name>        # Add new agent interactively
    23→openacp agents remove <name>     # Remove agent
    24→
    25→openacp channels list            # List configured channels
    26→openacp channels enable <name>   # Enable channel
    27→openacp channels disable <name>  # Disable channel
    28→
    29→openacp sessions list            # List active sessions
    30→openacp sessions cancel <id>     # Cancel a session
    31→```
    32→
    33→## Implementation
    34→
    35→- Built with a CLI framework (e.g., `commander`, `yargs`, or `citty`)
    36→- Reads/writes the same JSON config file
    37→- Communicates with running daemon via IPC (Unix socket or HTTP API)
    38→
    39→## Daemon Communication
    40→
    41→When `openacp start` runs, it starts the daemon process. CLI commands like `sessions list` communicate with the running daemon:
    42→
    43→- Option A: Unix socket (NDJSON, like Telegram-ACP)
    44→- Option B: HTTP API (same as Web UI API endpoints)
    45→
    46→Recommendation: HTTP API — reuse the same endpoints as Web UI, simpler to implement.
    47→

1→import { Bot } from 'grammy'
     2→import { ChannelAdapter, type OpenACPCore, type OutgoingMessage, type PermissionRequest, type NotificationMessage, type Session, log } from '@openacp/core'
     3→import type { TelegramChannelConfig } from './types.js'
     4→import { MessageDraft } from './streaming.js'
     5→import { ensureTopics, createSessionTopic, renameSessionTopic } from './topics.js'
     6→import { setupCommands } from './commands.js'
     7→import { PermissionHandler } from './permissions.js'
     8→import { spawnAssistant, handleAssistantMessage, redirectToAssistant } from './assistant.js'
     9→import { escapeHtml, formatToolCall, formatToolUpdate, formatPlan, formatUsage } from './formatting.js'
    10→
    11→export class TelegramAdapter extends ChannelAdapter {
    12→  private bot!: Bot
    13→  private telegramConfig: TelegramChannelConfig
    14→  private sessionDrafts: Map<string, MessageDraft> = new Map()
    15→  private toolCallMessages: Map<string, Map<string, number>> = new Map()  // sessionId → (toolCallId → msgId)
    16→  private permissionHandler!: PermissionHandler
    17→  private assistantSession: Session | null = null
    18→  private notificationTopicId!: number
    19→  private assistantTopicId!: number
    20→
    21→  constructor(core: OpenACPCore, config: TelegramChannelConfig) {
    22→    super(core, config as any)
    23→    this.telegramConfig = config
    24→  }
    25→
    26→  async start(): Promise<void> {
    27→    this.bot = new Bot(this.telegramConfig.botToken)
    28→
    29→    // Middleware: only accept messages from configured chatId
    30→    this.bot.use((ctx, next) => {
    31→      if (ctx.chat?.id !== this.telegramConfig.chatId) return
    32→      return next()
    33→    })
    34→
    35→    // Ensure system topics exist
    36→    const topics = await ensureTopics(
    37→      this.bot,
    38→      this.telegramConfig.chatId,
    39→      this.telegramConfig,
    40→      async (updates) => {
    41→        // Save topic IDs to config
    42→        await (this.core as OpenACPCore).configManager.save({
    43→          channels: { telegram: updates }
    44→        })
    45→      }
    46→    )
    47→    this.notificationTopicId = topics.notificationTopicId
    48→    this.assistantTopicId = topics.assistantTopicId
    49→
    50→    // Setup permission handler
    51→    this.permissionHandler = new PermissionHandler(
    52→      this.bot,
    53→      this.telegramConfig.chatId,
    54→      (sessionId) => (this.core as OpenACPCore).sessionManager.getSession(sessionId),
    55→      (notification) => this.sendNotification(notification),
    56→    )
    57→    this.permissionHandler.setupCallbackHandler()
    58→
    59→    // Setup commands
    60→    setupCommands(this.bot, this.core as OpenACPCore, this.telegramConfig.chatId)
    61→
    62→    // Setup message routing
    63→    this.setupRoutes()
    64→
    65→    // Start bot polling
    66→    this.bot.start({
    67→      allowed_updates: ['message', 'callback_query'],
    68→      onStart: () => log.info('Telegram bot started'),
    69→    })
    70→
    71→    // Spawn assistant (after bot is started so it can send messages)
    72→    try {
    73→      this.assistantSession = await spawnAssistant(
    74→        this.core as OpenACPCore,
    75→        this,
    76→        this.assistantTopicId,
    77→      )
    78→    } catch (err) {
    79→      log.error('Failed to spawn assistant:', err)
    80→    }
    81→  }
    82→
    83→  async stop(): Promise<void> {
    84→    if (this.assistantSession) {
    85→      await this.assistantSession.destroy()
    86→    }
    87→    await this.bot.stop()
    88→  }
    89→
    90→  private setupRoutes(): void {
    91→    this.bot.on('message:text', async (ctx) => {
    92→      const threadId = ctx.message.message_thread_id
    93→
    94→      // General topic or no thread → redirect to assistant
    95→      if (!threadId) {
    96→        const html = redirectToAssistant(this.telegramConfig.chatId, this.assistantTopicId)
    97→        await ctx.reply(html, { parse_mode: 'HTML' })
    98→        return
    99→      }

   102→      if (threadId === this.notificationTopicId) return

   105→      if (threadId === this.assistantTopicId) {

   107→        return
   108→      }
   109→
   110→      // Session topic → forward to core
   111→      await (this.core as OpenACPCore).handleMessage({
   112→        channelId: 'telegram',
   113→        threadId: String(threadId),
   114→        userId: String(ctx.from.id),
   115→        text: ctx.message.text,
   116→      })
   117→    })
   118→  }
   119→
   120→  // --- ChannelAdapter implementations ---
   121→
   122→  async sendMessage(sessionId: string, content: OutgoingMessage): Promise<void> {
   123→    const session = (this.core as OpenACPCore).sessionManager.getSession(sessionId)
   124→    if (!session) return

   134→      case 'text': {

1→# OpenACP
     2→
     3→Self-hosted bridge that lets you interact with AI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, etc.) from messaging platforms (Telegram, Discord, etc.) via the [Agent Client Protocol (ACP)](https://agentclientprotocol.org/).
     4→
     5→**One message, any channel, any agent.**
     6→
     7→## How It Works
     8→
     9→```
    10→You (Telegram / Discord / ...)
    11→  │
    12→  ▼
    13→OpenACP (ChannelAdapter)
    14→  │
    15→  ▼
    16→ACP Protocol (JSON-RPC over stdio)
    17→  │
    18→  ▼
    19→AI Agent subprocess (Claude Code, Codex, ...)
    20→```
    21→
    22→You send a message in Telegram → OpenACP forwards it to an AI coding agent via ACP → agent responds with text, code, tool calls → OpenACP streams the response back to your chat.
    23→
    24→## Features
    25→
    26→- **Multi-agent** — Switch between Claude Code, Codex, or any ACP-compatible agent
    27→- **Telegram integration** — Forum topics per session, real-time streaming, inline permission buttons
    28→- **Session management** — Multiple parallel sessions, prompt queue, auto-naming
    29→- **Assistant topic** — AI-powered help bot that guides you through creating sessions
    30→- **Notification topic** — Aggregated notifications with deep links
    31→- **Workspace management** — Named workspaces or custom paths
    32→- **Self-hosted** — Your keys, your data, your machine
    33→
    34→## Quick Start
    35→
    36→### Prerequisites
    37→
    38→- Node.js >= 20
    39→- pnpm
    40→- A Telegram bot token (from [@BotFather](https://t.me/BotFather))
    41→- A Telegram Supergroup with **Forum/Topics enabled**
    42→- At least one ACP agent installed (e.g., `claude-agent-acp`)
    43→
    44→### Install
    45→
    46→```bash
    47→git clone https://github.com/your-username/OpenACP.git
    48→cd OpenACP
    49→pnpm install
    50→pnpm build
    51→```
    52→
    53→### Configure
    54→
    55→Run once to generate the default config:
    56→
    57→```bash
    58→node packages/core/dist/main.js
    59→```
    60→
    61→Edit `~/.openacp/config.json`:
    62→
    63→```json
    64→{
    65→  "channels": {
    66→    "telegram": {
    67→      "enabled": true,
    68→      "botToken": "YOUR_BOT_TOKEN",
    69→      "chatId": -100YOUR_CHAT_ID
    70→    }
    71→  },
    72→  "agents": {
    73→    "claude": {
    74→      "command": "claude-agent-acp",
    75→      "args": []
    76→    }
    77→  },
    78→  "defaultAgent": "claude"
    79→}
    80→```
    81→
    82→### Setup Telegram
    83→
    84→1. Create a Supergroup in Telegram
    85→2. Enable **Topics** in group settings
    86→3. Add your bot as **admin** with **Manage Topics** permission
    87→4. Get the chat ID (use [@raw_data_bot](https://t.me/raw_data_bot) or similar)
    88→
    89→### Run
    90→
    91→```bash
    92→node packages/core/dist/main.js
    93→```
    94→
    95→OpenACP will auto-create two topics in your group:
    96→- **📋 Notifications** — aggregated alerts with deep links
    97→- **🤖 Assistant** — AI helper for managing sessions
    98→
    99→## Usage
   100→
   101→### Commands
   102→
   103→| Command | Description |
   104→|---------|-------------|
   105→| `/new [agent] [workspace]` | Create a new session |
   106→| `/new_chat` | New session, same agent & workspace |
   107→| `/cancel` | Cancel current session |
   108→| `/status` | Show session or system status |
   109→| `/agents` | List available agents |
   110→| `/help` | Show help |
   111→
   112→### Examples
   113→
   114→```
   115→/new claude my-app          → New session with Claude in ~/openacp-workspace/my-app/
   116→/new codex api-server       → New session with Codex in ~/openacp-workspace/api-server/
   117→/new claude ~/code/project  → New session with absolute path
   118→/new                        → New session with default agent and workspace
   119→```
   120→
   121→### Session Flow
   122→
   123→1. Type `/new claude my-project` — bot creates a new topic
   124→2. Send your coding request in the topic
   125→3. Agent responds with streaming text, tool calls, and code
   126→4. When agent needs permission (run command, edit file) → inline buttons appear
   127→5. Click Allow/Deny → agent continues
   128→6. `/cancel` to stop, or start a new topic with `/new`
   129→
   130→## Configuration
   131→
   132→Config file: `~/.openacp/config.json`
   133→
   134→```json
   135→{
   136→  "channels": {
   137→    "telegram": {
   138→      "enabled": true,
   139→      "botToken": "...",
   140→      "chatId": -1001234567890,
   141→      "notificationTopicId": null,
   142→      "assistantTopicId": null
   143→    }
   144→  },
   145→  "agents": {
   146→    "claude": {
   147→      "command": "claude-agent-acp",
   148→      "args": [],
   149→      "env": {}
   150→    },
   151→    "codex": {
   152→      "command": "codex",
   153→      "args": ["--acp"],
   154→      "env": {}
   155→    }
   156→  },
   157→  "defaultAgent": "claude",
   158→  "workspace": {
   159→    "baseDir": "~/openacp-workspace"
   160→  },
   161→  "security": {
   162→    "allowedUserIds": [],
   163→    "maxConcurrentSessions": 5,
   164→    "sessionTimeoutMinutes": 60
   165→  }
   166→}
   167→```
   168→
   169→### Environment Variables
   170→
   171→| Variable | Overrides |
   172→|----------|-----------|
   173→| `OPENACP_CONFIG_PATH` | Config file location |
   174→| `OPENACP_TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` | `channels.telegram.botToken` |
   175→| `OPENACP_TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID` | `channels.telegram.chatId` |
   176→| `OPENACP_DEFAULT_AGENT` | `defaultAgent` |
   177→| `OPENACP_DEBUG` | Enable debug logging (set to `1`) |
   178→
   179→## Project Structure
   180→
   181→```
   182→openacp/
   183→  packages/
   184→    core/                      → @openacp/core
   185→      src/
   186→        main.ts                → Entry point
   187→        core.ts                → OpenACPCore orchestrator
   188→        config.ts              → ConfigManager + Zod validation
   189→        session.ts             → Session (prompt queue, auto-name)
   190→        agent-instance.ts      → ACP SDK integration
   191→        channel.ts             → ChannelAdapter abstract class
   192→        types.ts               → Shared types
   193→    adapters/
   194→      telegram/                → @openacp/adapter-telegram
   195→        src/
   196→          adapter.ts           → TelegramAdapter
   197→          streaming.ts         → Real-time message streaming
   198→          commands.ts          → Bot commands
   199→          permissions.ts       → Permission inline buttons
   200→          assistant.ts         → AI assistant topic
   201→          formatting.ts        → Markdown → Telegram HTML
   202→          topics.ts            → Forum topic management
   203→```
   204→
   205→## Roadmap
   206→
   207→- **Phase 1** ✅ Core + Telegram + ACP agents
   208→- **Phase 2** — Web UI, CLI, Discord adapter, tunnel/file viewer
   209→- **Phase 3** — Agent skills as commands, session persistence
   210→- **Phase 4** — Voice control, file sharing
   211→- **Phase 5** — WhatsApp, agent chaining, plugin marketplace
   212→
   213→See [docs/specs/01-roadmap.md](docs/specs/01-roadmap.md) for details.
   214→
   215→## Adding a Channel Adapter
   216→
   217→Extend `ChannelAdapter` from `@openacp/core`:
   218→
   219→```typescript
   220→import { ChannelAdapter } from '@openacp/core'
   221→
   222→class MyAdapter extends ChannelAdapter {
   223→  async start() { /* connect to platform */ }
   224→  async stop() { /* disconnect */ }
   225→  async sendMessage(sessionId, content) { /* send to user */ }
   226→  async sendPermissionRequest(sessionId, request) { /* show buttons */ }
   227→  async sendNotification(notification) { /* notify user */ }
   228→  async createSessionThread(sessionId, name) { /* create thread */ }
   229→  async renameSessionThread(sessionId, name) { /* rename thread */ }
   230→}
   231→```
   232→
   233→## License
   234→
   235→AGPL-3.0
   236→

     2→
     3→> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.
     4→
     5→**Goal:** Build a self-hosted Telegram bot that bridges messaging to AI coding agents via ACP protocol.
     6→
     7→**Architecture:** Monorepo with `@openacp/core` (abstract channel adapter, session/agent managers, ACP SDK integration) and `@openacp/adapter-telegram` (grammy bot, forum topics, streaming). Core spawns ACP agent subprocesses, communicates via JSON-RPC over stdio using `@agentclientprotocol/sdk`.
     8→
     9→**Tech Stack:** TypeScript, Node.js, pnpm workspace, @agentclientprotocol/sdk, grammy, Zod, nanoid
    10→
    11→**Spec:** `docs/specs/phase1/`
    12→
    13→---
    14→
    15→## File Map
    16→
    17→### packages/core/
    18→
    19→| File | Responsibility |
    20→|------|----------------|
    21→| `package.json` | Package config, dependencies |
    22→| `tsconfig.json` | TypeScript config extending base |
    23→| `src/types.ts` | All shared interfaces/types |
    24→| `src/log.ts` | Simple logger utility |
    25→| `src/config.ts` | ConfigManager + Zod schema + workspace resolution |
    26→| `src/channel.ts` | ChannelAdapter abstract class |
    27→| `src/streams.ts` | Node→Web stream converters |
